comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD attribute their fiscal 2024 R&D expense increases primarily to compensation-related factors. QCOM cites a $113 million increase in share-based compensation and a $66 million increase in deferred compensation revaluation, partially offset by restructuring-driven cost decreases. AMD attributes its $584 million (10%) increase to higher employee-related costs resulting from headcount growth to support its AI strategy. While both mention compensation/headcount, AMD's increase is driven by volume (headcount/AI strategy) rather than specific accounting revaluations or restructuring offsets seen at QCOM.

sentences.text: The increase in research and development expenses in fiscal 2024 was due to:
+ $113 million increase in share-based compensation expense

+ $66 million increase in expenses driven by revaluation of our deferred compensation obligation (which resulted in a corresponding increase in net gains on deferred compensation plan assets within investment and other income, net due to the revaluation of the related assets)
Research and development expenses of $6.5 billion in 2024 increased by $584 million, or 10%, compared to $5.9 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.

comparisons.comparison: QCOM and AVGO both disclose R&D expense increases driven by higher compensation and stock-based compensation. QCOM reports a smaller increase driven by $113 million in share-based compensation and $66 million in deferred compensation revaluation. A key difference is AVGO's growth is heavily tied to acquisition integration (VMware), whereas QCOM explicitly cites restructuring actions to reduce wireless/IC development costs, partially offsetting its compensation-driven increases.
